Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:10:1.hebrew: אלא למ"ד אין בו מאי דיו - מאי רבותיה דאצטריך למתני דיו? ליתני אומר הוא וחומשו כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:10:1.english: But according to the one who says "it does not have," what [is the meaning of] "it is sufficient" - What is its novelty that it needed to teach "it is sufficient"? Let it teach [simply], "He says, 'It and its fifth,'" etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:11:1.hebrew: חומשא מלגיו - על שוה עשרים זוז, מוסיף ארבע, שהן חומשו של קרן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:11:1.english: One-fifth from within - For [something] worth twenty zuz, he adds four [zuz], which are a fifth of the principal.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:11:2.hebrew: או חומשא מלבר - על ארבעה רבעי' מוסיף החמישית מן החוץ, דהוו להו לעשרים זוז חמשא זוזי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:11:2.english: Or one-fifth from without - Upon four quarters, he adds the fifth from the outside, so that for twenty zuz [it] is five zuz.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:11:3.english: The owners say for twenty - Regarding one who consecrates [property] and redeems his consecrated property, we learned it in Tractate Arakhin (27a).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:11:4.hebrew: מפני שמוסיפין חומש - ועשרים שלהן הוו כ"ה, דאילו שאר כל אדם לא יוסיף חומש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:11:4.english: Because they add a fifth - And their twenty become twenty-five, whereas any other person will not add a fifth.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:1:1.hebrew: ואפי' בירושלים - שאין מעשר טהור נפדה שם, דכתיב (דברים יד) כי ירחק ממך [וגו'] ונתת בכסף, ולא כשהיה בירושלים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:1:1.english: And even in Jerusalem - For ritually pure [second] tithe is not redeemed there, as it is written (Deuteronomy 14[:24–25]): "When [the place] is too far from you [etc.] then you shall turn [it] into money" — and not when it was [already] in Jerusalem.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:2:1.hebrew: בלקוח - מעשר זה, ולא הוא עצמו היה מעשר, אלא צרכי סעודה שלקח בירושלים בכסף מעשר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:2:1.english: With [something] purchased - [That is,] this tithe [under discussion], and it itself was not [actual] tithe, rather [it was] meal provisions that he purchased in Jerusalem with tithe money.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:2:2.english: Must be buried - For he holds [that] it is not strong enough to take hold of its redemption.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:3:1.hebrew: אלא לעולם בטהור - בין מעשר בין לקוח, ודקאמר ״נעייליה וניכליה״:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:3:1.english: Rather, actually, [it is] with regard to [produce that is] ritually pure - whether [second-]tithe [produce] or [food] purchased [with second-tithe money]; and as for what [the Gemara] asked, "Let him bring it in and eat it":

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:3:2.hebrew: מאי יצא - נמי דקאמר, דנפול מחיצות חומת ירושלים, ושוב אין מעשר נאכל שם עד שיעמדו מחיצות, דבעינן "לפני ה' תאכלנו" (שם יב). ובפדייה נמי לא, דקלטוהו מחיצות מלפדותו עוד משנכנס לתוכו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:3:2.english: What [does] "exited" - that it also states [mean]? [It means] that the partitions of the wall of Jerusalem fell, and [second] tithe can no longer be eaten there until [the] partitions stand [again], for we require, "before the Lord shall you eat it" (ibid. 12). And [it is] also not [permitted] through redemption, for the partitions have taken hold of it [to prevent it] from being redeemed anymore once it entered inside it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:4:1.english: But doesn't Rava say - In Tractate Makkot (20a).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:4:2.hebrew: מחיצה לאכול דאורייתא מחיצה לקלוט דרבנן - מחיצה שנאמרה בתורה לא הוזכרה אלא לאכול בתוכה, ושאמרו במשנה מחיצות קולטות אותם מלפדות עוד אם יצא, דרבנן היא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:4:2.english: A partition to eat [is] by Torah law, a partition to gather [is] by rabbinic law - The partition that is stated in the Torah was mentioned only [in order] to eat inside it; and [that] which they said in the Mishnah, [that] partitions gather them [preventing them] from being redeemed any longer if [the produce] went out, is by rabbinic law.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:4:3.hebrew: וכי גזור רבנן כו' - לאו רבא קאמר לה, אלא המקשה קאמר: מדאמר רבא קליטת מחיצות מדרבנן בעלמא היא, והשתא דנפול מחיצות ליתא לההיא גזירה, דכי גזור רבנן היכא דאיתנהו וזה הוציא את המעשר לחוץ, אבל כי ליתנהו לא גזור. הלכך, ניפרקיה, ואמאי בטלי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:4:3.english: And when the Sages issued a decree, etc. - Rava did not say this; rather, the questioner is saying [it]: Since Rava said [that] the gathering [capacity] of partitions is merely by rabbinic law, now that the partitions have fallen, that decree does not apply, for when the Sages issued a decree, [it was] where [the partitions] exist and this [person] took the tithe outside, but where they do not exist, they did not issue a decree. Therefore, let us redeem it, and why are they annulled?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:4:4.hebrew: ומשני לא פלוג רבנן - בין יוצא מתוכן לנפלו, דקליטת מחיצות גזרו בסתם, בין איתנהו בין ליתנהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:4:4.english: And [the Gemara] answers: The Sages did not distinguish - between [produce] going out from within them and [a case where] they fell, for they issued a general decree regarding the gathering [effect] of partitions, whether they are [intact] or whether they are not [intact].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:5:1.hebrew: רב הונא ברבי יהודה אמר - הא דאותבת לחזקיה מרישא דקתני "באיזה מעשר אמרו? שאין בו שוה פרוטה", וקשיא לך "ליעבד כדחזקיה" — לא קשיא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:5:1.english: Rav Huna bar Rabbi Yehuda said - That which you raised as an objection to Chizkiyah from the first clause [of the baraita], which teaches: "Regarding which [second] tithe did they say [this]? One that is not worth a peruta," and it was difficult for you: "Let him act in accordance with Chizkiyah" — it is not difficult:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:5:2.english: It teaches one [case]: [second tithe] that is not worth a perutah, which entered Jerusalem and exited - For the taking hold of the walls [of Jerusalem] prevents it from being redeemed any further onto the first coins.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:5:3.english: And let us return and bring it in and eat it - In Jerusalem, with its mixture.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:5:4.english: Where the partitions fell - And this is [the meaning of] "exited" that [it] teaches.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:7:1.hebrew: אפי' יש בו שוה פרוטה - נמי לאו בר אכילה ולאו בר חילול הוא, ואמאי תני: "באיזה מעשר אמרו? בשאין בו שוה פרוטה כו'":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:7:1.english: Even [if] it has the value of a peruta - [it is] also neither fit for eating nor fit for redemption; so why does [the Tanna] teach, "Of which tithe did they state [this]? Of [one] that does not have the value of a peruta," etc.?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:7:2.hebrew: לא מבעיא יש בו - דכיון דבר פדייה הוא, חיילא עליו קליטת מחיצות דרבנן, ולא מיפרוק תו. אבל אין בו, אימא בכה"ג לא לגזור רבנן קליטת מחיצות לפדייה, דמילתא דלא שכיח היא לחללו על מעות הראשונות, וניעבד ליה כדחזקיה, קמ"ל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:7:2.english: It is not necessary [to state that if] it has [the value of a peruta] - For since it is subject to redemption, the rabbinic taking hold by the partitions takes effect upon it, and it can no longer be redeemed. But [where] it does not have [the value of a peruta], I might say that in such a case the Rabbis did not decree the taking hold by the partitions with respect to redemption, because it is an uncommon matter to redeem it onto the first coins, and we should act regarding it in accordance with Chizkiyah; [therefore,] it teaches us [that the decree still applies].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:8:1.hebrew: פרט לשאין בו שוה פרוטה - שאינו בכלל גאולה, ולימדך שאינה תופסת פרוטה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:8:1.english: To exclude [second tithe] that does not have the value of a peruta - For it is not included in [the law of] redemption, and [Scripture] taught you that [redemption] does not take effect [with] a peruta.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:8:2.hebrew: רב אמי אמר אין בו שוה פרוטה - שנינו, אבל אם יש בו שוה פרוטה, בר גאולה הוא ותופס פדיונו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:8:2.english: Rav Ami says: [It] does not have the value of a peruta - [this is what] we learned [in the baraita], but if it has the value of a peruta, it is subject to redemption and its redemption takes effect.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:8:3.hebrew: ורב אסי אמר אין בחומשו שוה פרוטה - שנינו, דלאו בר גאולה הוא עד שיהא בו שוה ארבע פרוטות, כדי שיהא ראוי לתוספת חומש דכתיב בהאי קרא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:8:3.english: And Rav Asi says: Its fifth does not [have] the value of a peruta - [So] we learned [it], that it is not subject to redemption unless it has the value of four perutot, so that it will be fit for the addition of a fifth that is written in this verse.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:9:1.hebrew: דיו שיאמר כו' - כדחזקיה, ולא אמרינן ימתין עד שיעלנו לירושלים או ימתין עד שיצרפנו עם אחר, דכיון דבחומשיה ליכא [פרוטה], לא קחשיב ודיו בכך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 53b:9:1.english: It is sufficient that he say, etc. - [This is] in accordance with Chizkiyah, and we do not say [that] he must wait until he brings it up to Jerusalem or wait until he combines it with other [produce]; for since there is not [a peruta] in its [additional] fifth, it is not considered significant, and this is sufficient for him.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 53b:2:1.hebrew: כרבי יהודה דאמר יקבר - בספרי מפיק טעמא, משום דכתיב "הכסף" — כסף ראשון ולא כסף שני. וא״ת: דבריש פירקין (בבא מציעא דף מה.) אמרינן "כסף ראשון ואפי' כסף שני"? וי״ל: דה״מ כסף על כסף, אבל לחלל ב' פעמים פירות על כסף — לא. וא״ת: דבפרק שלישי דמעשר שני (מ״י) תנן: "אמרו לו לר' יהודה: ומה מעשר שנטמא נפדה, לקוח לא כל שכן? אמר להם: לא, אם אמרתם במעשר שנפדה טהור ברחוק מקום, תאמרו בלקוח שאינו נפדה כו'"; אם כן, טעמא אחרינא אית ליה, ולמה לי קרא בספרי? וי״ל: דאסמכתא בעלמא הוא, אי נמי טרח וכתב לה קרא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 53b:2:1.english: [The baraita is] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who says [it] must be buried - In the Sifri, [the Tanna] derives the reason from the fact that it is written, "the money" — [meaning] first money, and not second money. And if you will ask: At the beginning of our chapter (Bava Metzia 45a), we say, "first money, and even second money"? One can answer that this applies [only to redeeming] money onto money, but to deconsecrate produce onto money twice — no [that is not permitted]. And if you will ask: In the third chapter of Ma'aser Sheni (Mishnah 10), we learned: "They said to Rabbi Yehuda: If [second-]tithe [produce] that became ritually impure is redeemed, should [food] acquired [with second-tithe money] not all the more so [be redeemed]? He said to them: No; if you say [this] regarding [second-]tithe [produce], which is redeemed [even when] ritually pure in a distant place [from Jerusalem], will you say [the same] regarding [food] acquired [with second-tithe money], which is not redeemed, etc."; if so, he has another reason, so why do I need the verse in the Sifri? One can answer that it is merely an asmakhta [a scriptural support], or alternatively, [Scripture] took the trouble to write a verse for it.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 53b:3:1.hebrew: אפילו לא יצא נמי - מעיקרא דשני בשנטמא, ה"מ למפרך הכי, אלא דעדיפא מיניה פריך:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 53b:3:1.english: Even [if it] did not exit as well - Originally, when [the Gemara] answered [that it refers to] when it became ritually impure, it could have raised this [objection], except that it raised a stronger one than it.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 53b:4:1.hebrew: לא פלוג רבנן - תימה, דבסוף פרק חלק (סנהדרין ד' קיג.) משני: כי גזרו רבנן — כי איתנהו למחיצות, ולא קאמר דלא פלוג רבנן כדקאמר הכא. ולא קשה מידי: דהתם קאי אמאי דקאמר: אלא דעיר הנדחת, ואסקוה לירושלים והיה שם בשעת גמר דין — ליתאכיל, דהא קלטוהו מחיצות וה"ל שלל ירושלים בשעת גמר דין כו', ומסיק: לעולם בטהור, ואסקיה לירושלים ונגמר הדין דעיר הנדחת, ודקא קשיא לך "ליתאכיל" — כגון דנפול מחיצות אמר (אחר) גמר דין, וכדרבא דאמר מחיצה לקלוט דרבנן. שלא לפדות — אפילו נפול מחיצה, דלא פלוג רבנן כדקאמר בשמעתין; דכיון דלקלוט לא הוי אלא מדרבנן, מן התורה חל עליו גמר דין אפילו לא נפול מחיצה כלל, כיון שיכול לאוכלו אם ירצה, ולא מיקרי נמי שלל ירושלי' כיון שיכול להוציאו ולפדותו, אלא דרבנן אמור מחיצה לקלוט, אפילו לקרות שלל ירושלים ולאכול, דהעמידו דבריהם על דין תורה. אהא מסיים: כי גזרו רבנן — היכא דאיתנהו למחיצות; פירוש: לא העמידו דבריהם על דין תורה למיקרי שלל ירושלים ולאכול אלא כי איתנהו למחיצות ולא נפול כלל, אבל נפול מחיצות אחר גמר דין — לא גזור רבנן להעמיד דבריהם על דין תורה לקרות שלל ירושלים ולאכול, אע"ג דבשעת גמר דין קלטוהו מחיצות, כיון דנפול מחיצות אחר גמר דין. אבל אי נפול מחיצות קודם גמר דין, אע"ג דלא הוי שלל ירושלים, מ"מ לא חל עליו גמר דין, דה"ל כגבולים, וה"ל שלל שמים כיון שאינו ראוי לאכול ולא לפדות, כדאמר בשמעתין דלא פלוג רבנן, ויעלוהו כשיעשו מחיצות. א"נ, דוקא מיירי בנפול מחיצות קודם גמר דין, ולא הוי כמו בגבולים: דכיון שהיה ראוי לאכלו שעה אחת הוה ליה ממון הדיוט, ושלל ירושלים לא הוי כיון דנפול מחיצות בשעת גמר דין; אבל נפול מחיצות אחר גמר דין — כיון דהוי שלל ירושלים בשעת גמר דין, תו לא פקע. והשתא אתי שפיר טפי בפשיטות: כי איתנהו בשעת גמר דין — גזור למיהוי שלל ירושלים; כי ליתנהו בשעת גמר דין — לא גזור. ואם תאמר: דמשמע דיגנזו משום דחל עלייהו גמר דין, אבל היכא דלא חל עלייהו גמר דין — יאכלו אם תבנה החומה, והא אמרינן בפרק קדשי קדשים (זבחים דף נט.): כשהיה מזבח שלם ונפגם ונבנה — אין חוזרין ונראין! וי"ל: דדוקא זבחים שעושין מהם עבודות, אבל מעשר, או בשר זבח לאחר העבודה, או שירי מנחה — חוזרין ונראין:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 53b:4:1.english: The Sages did not distinguish - This is astonishing, for at the end of chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 113a) [the Gemara] answers: "When the Sages issued a decree, [it was only] where there are [intact] partitions," and it does not say that the Sages did not distinguish, as it says here! However, there is no difficulty at all: for there it refers to what [the Gemara] says: "Rather, [it is] of a subverted city, and they brought it up to Jerusalem and it was there at the time of the final verdict — let it be eaten, since the partitions have gathered it and it has become the spoil of Jerusalem at the time of the final verdict," etc., and [the Gemara] concludes: "Actually, [it is] with ritually pure [produce], and they brought it up to Jerusalem and the final verdict of the subverted city was issued; and as for what you asked: 'Let it be eaten!' — [it is] a case where the partitions fell after [printed: amar] the final verdict, and [it is] in accordance with Rava, who says that a partition to gather is rabbinic." [As for not being able] to redeem [it], [that applies] even if the partition fell, because the Sages did not distinguish, as [the Gemara] says in our passage; for since "gathering" is only rabbinic, by Torah law the final verdict takes effect on it even if the partitions did not fall at all, since one could eat it if he wished, nor is it called the spoil of Jerusalem since he can take it out and redeem it — rather, the Sages said that a partition gathers, even to the extent of calling it the spoil of Jerusalem and eating [it], for they established their words like Torah law. Upon this [the Gemara there] concludes: "When the Sages issued a decree, [it was] where there are [intact] partitions." Explanation: they did not establish their words like Torah law to call it the spoil of Jerusalem and eat [it] except when there are [intact] partitions and they did not fall at all; but if the partitions fell after the final verdict, the Sages did not decree to establish their words like Torah law to call it the spoil of Jerusalem and eat [it] — even though at the time of the final verdict the partitions had gathered it — since the partitions fell after the final verdict. However, if the partitions fell before the final verdict, even though it is not the spoil of Jerusalem, nevertheless the final verdict did not take effect on it, for it is like [produce in] the outlying borders, and it is "spoil of Heaven" since it is fit neither to be eaten nor to be redeemed, as [the Gemara] says in our passage that the Sages did not distinguish, and they may bring it up [to be eaten] when the partitions are rebuilt. Alternatively, [Sanhedrin 113a] is specifically speaking of where the partitions fell before the final verdict, and it is not like [produce] in the outlying borders: for since it was fit to be eaten for one moment, it is [considered] ordinary property, and it is not the spoil of Jerusalem since the partitions had fallen at the time of the final verdict; whereas if the partitions fell after the final verdict, since it was the spoil of Jerusalem at the time of the final verdict, it no longer ceases [to be so]. And now it works out much more simply: when [the partitions] are present at the time of the final verdict, they decreed [the produce] to be the spoil of Jerusalem; when they are not present at the time of the final verdict, they did not decree [this]. And if you say: It implies that they must be hidden away because the final verdict took effect on them, whereas where the final verdict did not take effect on them, they may be eaten if the wall is rebuilt — yet we say in chapter Kodshei Kodashim (Zevachim 59a): "When the altar was whole, and became damaged, and was rebuilt, [disqualified offerings] do not return and become fit"! One can answer: That applies specifically to sacrifices with which [Temple] services are performed; but second tithe, or the meat of a sacrifice after the service, or the remainder of a meal offering, do return and become fit.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 53b:5:1.hebrew: דנפול מחיצות - פי': רוב מחיצות, דאי נפול מקצתם, אע"ג דאסור לטלטל בשבת, מ"מ מקרי מחיצה לענין אכילת מעשר וקדשים קלים, כדאמרינן ריש פרק אלו דברים (פסחים דף סו. ושם ד"ה תוחב ודף סז), דההיא שמעתתא דהלל צריך להעמיד אחר שנפרצו בה פרצות — לכך לא היו יכולין להוליך סכיניהם בשבת לעזרה לשחוט פסחיהם, דקודם שנפרצו היו מותרים לטלטל, כדאמר רבי יוחנן (עירובין דף ו:): "ירושלים, אלמלא דלתותיה נעולות בלילה, חייבין עליה משום רה"ר", ואעפ"כ בלילה היו אוכלין פסחיהם:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 53b:5:1.english: "Where the partitions fell" - Explanation: [This means] the majority of the partitions [fell], for if [only] part of them fell, even though it is forbidden to carry on Shabbat, nevertheless it is considered a partition with regard to eating [second] tithe and offerings of lesser holiness, as we say at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] Eilu Devarim (Pesachim 66a, and there s.v. Tochev, and 67), for that discussion of Hillel must be established [as referring to a time] after breaches were made in [the city wall] — therefore they were not able to carry their knives on Shabbat to the Temple courtyard to slaughter their Passover offerings, for before [the walls] were breached, they were permitted to carry, as Rabbi Yochanan said (Eruvin 6b): "Jerusalem — were it not that its doors are locked at night, one would be liable on its account for [carrying in] a public domain," and even so, at night they would eat their Passover offerings.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 53b:7:1.hebrew: אין בו שוה פרוטה - אין תופס פדיון, ולא בעי למדרש: "אין בו שוה פרוטה — אין מוסיף חומש, אבל פדיון תופס", דסברא לאוקמא מיעוטא בגופה ולא בחומש, דפחות משוה פרוטה לא חשיב ממון לתפוס פדיון; אבל למ"ד "אין בחומשו", קשה, דטפי הוה ליה למדרש דאינו מוסיף חומש:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 53b:7:1.english: Does not have the value of a peruta - Redemption does not take effect [on it], and [the Gemara] does not want to expound [the verse as meaning]: "[If] it does not have the value of a peruta, he does not add a fifth, but redemption does take effect," because it is logical to apply the exclusion to [the produce] itself and not to the fifth, since less than the value of a peruta is not considered money for redemption to take effect. However, according to the one who says [it refers to where] "its fifth does not have [the value of a peruta]," it is difficult, for it would be more reasonable to expound [the verse] that he does not add a fifth.
